title: Angular-mode misalignment relic (fails at condensate scale) vs amplitude-mode freeze-out (viable)

G1_scaling.note: Omega ∝ m_a^{1/2} f^2 theta^2 (x4 mass->x2, x2 f->x4, x2 theta->x4)
G1_scaling._desc: misalignment scaling Omega ∝ m^0.5 f^2 theta^2

G2_condensate_scale_fails.note: f=v/2=123 GeV needs trans-Planckian m_a -> misalignment fails at the condensate scale

G3_light_mode_underproduces.note: light angular mode (small lambda6, f=123 GeV) under-produces by ~15 orders

G4_axion_window_needs_high_f.note: a light (~ueV) angular mode reaches Omega_DM only at f~10^13 GeV, far above the condensate

G5_freezeout_viable.note: heavy amplitude mode (~TeV, EW coupling) hits Omega h^2~0.12 -> the viable relic route
G5_freezeout_viable._desc: heavy amplitude mode freeze-out reaches Omega_DM

verdict: Standard misalignment with the condensate's NATURAL decay constant (f ~ v/2 = 123 GeV) badly UNDER-produces: Omega ∝ f^2, so a low-scale f needs either a trans-Planckian mass (light mode) or relies on the heavy amplitude-mode freeze-out instead. A light axion-like angular mode reaches Omega_DM only if f is pushed to ~10^15-10^16 GeV (intermediate/GUT), far above the E_g condensate scale. The relic obstruction is therefore SHARPENED, not closed: misalignment alone fails by the f-scale gap. The heavy AMPLITUDE mode via thermal freeze-out DOES reach Omega_DM in the WIMP window, so the E_g sector's dark-matter relic is the heavy amplitude mode, not the light angular one (updating the F197 candidate identification).
